name: Blink
funFact: Humans blink around 15–20 times per minute — so often that our eyes are closed for roughly 10% of our waking hours.

name: Heartbeat
funFact: The human heart beats about 100,000 times a day — over a lifetime, that's roughly 3 billion heartbeats.

name: Coffee break
funFact: The formal coffee break was introduced in 1902 by the Stoughton, Wisconsin city council — it's been legally protected in some workplaces ever since.

name: TV episode
funFact: The 45-minute TV drama format was designed around the commercial break structure of 1960s American broadcasting — and has barely changed since.

name: Song
funFact: The average pop song has gotten shorter since streaming — from 3m 50s in 2013 to under 3m 20s by 2020, partly because artists get paid per stream after 30 seconds.

name: Power nap
funFact: NASA research found that a 26-minute nap improved pilot performance by 34% and alertness by 100%.

name: Toilet scroll
description: Average phone session in the bathroom ≈ 8 minutes.
funFact: A study found 75% of people use their phone in the bathroom — and the average session is 8 minutes, longer than most news articles take to read.

name: Average commute
exampleMeme: The time you spend regretting your life choices.
funFact: The average commute in the US is 27.6 minutes — adding up to about 9 full days per year spent getting to and from work.

name: Work day
funFact: The 8-hour work day was championed by Robert Owen in 1817 with the slogan: 8 hours labour, 8 hours recreation, 8 hours rest.

name: Lunar month
funFact: Every calendar system in history has had to grapple with the fact that 12 lunar months is 11 days shorter than a solar year — solved differently by different cultures.

name: Week
funFact: The 7-day week has no astronomical basis — it was invented in ancient Mesopotamia around 600 BC and spread so universally that no culture has successfully replaced it.

name: Month
funFact: No month is exactly the same length — February's 28 days exist because Roman emperor Augustus stole a day from it to make his month (August) as long as Julius Caesar's July.

name: Year
funFact: A year is not exactly 365 days — it's 365.25 days, which is why we add a leap day every 4 years. Even then we over-correct, so century years skip the leap day unless divisible by 400.

name: Decade
exampleMeme: Long enough to regret a haircut.
funFact: Humans are notoriously bad at remembering when things happened within a decade — a phenomenon called 'telescoping', where distant events feel more recent than they are.

name: 100m sprint
funFact: Usain Bolt's world record 100m time of 9.58s means he averaged 37.6 km/h — his top speed mid-race was 44.7 km/h.

name: Mars day
funFact: A day on Mars (called a 'sol') is just 37 minutes longer than an Earth day — making Mars the most Earth-like planet in terms of day length.

name: Dog year
funFact: The '7 dog years per human year' rule is a myth — dogs age rapidly in their first 2 years, then slow down. A 1-year-old dog is more like a 15-year-old human.

name: Human lifespan
description: Average human lifespan ≈ 72 years ≈ 2.27 billion seconds.
funFact: If you're 30 years old, you've lived approximately 946,080,000 seconds — nearly a billion. You'll hit the billion-second mark at around 31 years and 8 months.

name: Since the dinosaurs
description: Time since non-avian dinosaur extinction ≈ 66 million years.
funFact: Birds are technically dinosaurs — the Velociraptor was more closely related to a modern pigeon than to a T-Rex. So dinosaurs didn't go extinct; they're outside your window.

name: Age of the universe
description: Age of the observable universe ≈ 13.8 billion years.
funFact: If the entire history of the universe were compressed into one calendar year, modern humans wouldn't appear until 11:59:59 PM on December 31st — the last second.

name: Light to the Moon
description: Time for light to travel Earth to Moon ≈ 1.28 s.
funFact: During the Apollo missions, the 1.28-second one-way delay meant every question from mission control waited 2.56 seconds for an answer — clearly audible in the recordings.

name: Gym session
exampleMeme: One session closer to being mysterious.

name: Bad meeting
